sectionPath: 6. Record what was not decided
task_d40e199c1a8356aba0a83066.description: 6.1 Record that rows already written in local time are NOT migrated by this change, and that their originating zone was never stored, so no backfill can be correct without an assumption

evidence.summary: Recorded decision/non-decision: rows already persisted in bare local time (no Z) are NOT migrated by this change. The change only alters the serializer going forward (new rows end in Z); no migration script, backfill, or timezone field was added (rg for migrate/backfill/timezone in lib returns only the pre-existing helper naming, nothing that rewrites historical rows). Because the pre-fix serializer emitted local DateTime.now() with no zone suffix, the originating zone of each historical row was never stored, so any backfill would have to assume a fixed zone and could not be correct in general. Left as an explicit non-decision for the user; no retroactive rewrite is attempted.

sectionPath: 6. Record what was not decided
task_9e9db4f6c329b06c8b5002db.description: 6.2 Record the open question of whether readers should reject or accept a basis-less string

evidence.summary: Open question recorded (not decided here): whether readers should REJECT or ACCEPT a basis-less (no-Z) string. Current behaviour is ACCEPT: every reader uses generic DateTime.parse(json[...]), which silently accepts both a Z-suffixed and a basis-less string (Dart treats a no-zone string as local). That means legacy bare-local rows still parse, which is what lets 6.1's no-backfill stance hold. Whether to instead make readers reject basis-less strings (fail loudly on old rows) is deliberately left open for the user - it trades backward-compat for loudness and is out of scope for this change. No reader was changed to reject; the question is documented, not resolved.

sectionPath: 6. Record what was not decided
task_ce62e3fa68c870d5e1dc188c.description: 6.3 Record whether the unify-before-extract ordering should be mechanically enforced or left as a written requirement

evidence.summary: Recorded (not decided): the unify-before-extract ordering is currently enforced ONLY as a WRITTEN requirement (tasks.md 4.1) plus the actual git commit order a515b76 (unify) preceding a97d5bf (extract). There is NO mechanical guard - no lint, no test that fails if extraction is attempted on a non-UTC site, no CI check that asserts the ordering. Whether to add a mechanical enforcement (e.g. a guard test that asserts every toIso8601String call site already routes through a UTC-normalizing helper before the helper may exist, or a review bot rule) is left open for the user. Nothing mechanical was added; the ordering relies on discipline and git history, which is documented here.

sectionPath: 6. Record what was not decided
task_7b2ae737979f3adc78ca975b.description: 6.4 Do not resolve 6.1-6.3 unilaterally; they are for the user

evidence.summary: Confirmed: 6.1-6.3 were NOT resolved unilaterally - they remain open, recorded, and left for the user. 6.1 (no backfill of legacy local rows), 6.2 (accept vs reject basis-less readers) and 6.3 (mechanical vs written enforcement of unify-before-extract) are all documented as non-decisions/open questions in their respective evidence and were not acted on. No migration code, no reader behavior change, and no mechanical guard were added to resolve them on the agent's own judgement. The production fix (a515b76/a97d5bf) and the gates stand; git status is clean. These three questions are explicitly handed back to the user to decide.
